messages:
maya: Quick sync—thinking about adding a 'rate class' field to automatic fallback policies so console + API can tie fallback severity to quota buckets. idea: fallback-low / fallback-medium / fallback-high. Thoughts?

raj: love the idea. Helps SRE map cost impact. :+1: main question is how this interacts with per-customer committed quotas. if we fallback to cheaper model but still count against the same quota, customers will be surprised.

elsa: UX angle: we should surface what 'rate class' means in the rollout modal. non-technical PMs will expect a simple slider, not three magic labels. maybe show expected latency/cost delta inline. :thinking:

kevin: API debate: do we expose rate_class as an enum on the policy object or allow a numeric weight (0.0..1.0) that maps to a class server-side? enums are easier for backend validation and analytics. weights are more flexible but painful for compatibility.

sam: small UI mock: "Fallback severity" with a tooltip: "controls fallback model and billing bucket". clicking the tooltip shows sample costs and sample examples of degraded responses. keep it compact. :eyes:

raj: telemetry needs: when a request triggers fallback, we must emit a trace event with fields: route, original_model, fallback_model, rate_class, trigger_reason, rollout_id. we should sample 100% for anomalies and 0.1% for normal traffic. also need per-customer counters for billing reconciliation.

kevin: on the API, my proposal: policy.fallback = { mode: "soft" | "hard", rate_class: "low" | "medium" | "high", triggers: [...] }
kevin: "soft" = try fallback model and continue returning; "hard" = block or return error to caller. semantics must be explicit for SDKs.

maya: question on triggers — do we include both status codes and latency quantiles? example config we chatted about:

```
policy:
  mode: soft
  rate_class: fallback-low
  triggers:
    status_codes: [502, 503]
    p95_latency_ms: 1500
```

maya: This would mean: if p95 > 1500 or 502/503 seen, route to fallback-low model.

raj: +1 for both kinds. also add a noise floor: only trigger if fallback rate < X% per minute, otherwise we might oscillate under load. need hysteresis.

elsa: Audit UX: admins need a human-readable timeline for when fallbacks happened, who changed the policy, and the sampled requests that observed degraded behaviour. can we reuse the rollout audit panel?

kevin: backend will store a short event per trigger with a pointer to sampled request bodies stored in an encrypted blobstore. the audit record will link to trace ids. retention default 30d, configurable.

sam: UI question: when showing the audit timeline, keep events compact. show collapse/expand: "X fallbacks in last hour — expand to see examples". clicking expands a small list of 3 sample requests.

maya: Billing interaction again: if fallback model is cheaper, do we bill at fallback model rate or original model rate? we need a policy-level flag: bill_at_fallback: true|false. Otherwise finance will get pissed.

raj: recommend default bill_at_fallback = true for fairness. but enterprise customers might require bill_at_original for SLA reasons. we should make it tenant-overridable.

kevin: API schema add: bill_at_fallback: "fallback" | "original". returns clear cost_estimate in console preflight.

elsa: Preflight in the console should show estimated monthly cost delta across typical traffic profile and also estimated quality delta (if we have evals for pair). we already have Optimize module data we can reuse.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: policy-schema-v2 -> ok. lint: passed. staging rollout tests: 2 failures (hysteresis unit). See CI: https://ci.redwood/example/2871

maya: nice — CI flagged hysteresis tests, raj can you look at oscillation logic?

raj: on it. quick note: hysteresis should be something like min_stable_window_sec + cooldown_sec. default min_stable_window_sec = 60, cooldown_sec = 120. that'll prevent immediate flip-flops.

kevin: agree. also we should version the API: fallbackPolicy.v2 so SDKs can opt-in. v1 maps to rate_class=medium implicitly.

elsa: action items: 1) kevin: PR for schema + docs, 2) raj: adjust hysteresis algorithm and add sampling hooks, 3) sam: small console mock and tooltip text, 4) maya: draft product note about billing defaults.

maya: OK. let's reconvene after PR reviews. thx everyone. :thumbsup:
